- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥1.0) in recent days, reduce forecast overshoots, especially after spikes; model tends to overreact.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤-1.0) or mixed, model often underestimates downside risk; adjust downward bias by 3–5% relative to recent mean.
- When sentiment flips from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 5–7 days, model fails to adjust quickly; apply lag correction: shift forecast 1–2 days backward for volatility spikes.
- Mean reversion is stronger in high-sentiment periods; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–4% per day until convergence.
- In high-sentiment, low-forecast-variance periods, model tends to overpredict; cap forecast at 1.2x recent 14-day moving average to avoid overextension.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “bullish → bearish” transitions, model overcorrects; apply smoothing: average 3–5 prior forecasts before final output.
